newsitem.title: USA: White House says it regrets Whitewater ruling.
newsitem.headline: White House says it regrets Whitewater ruling.

text.p: The White House on Monday said it regretted the Supreme Court's rejection of an appeal involving turning over notes taken by one of its lawyers about a conversation with first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton.

"We continue to believe that government lawyers must be allowed to have confidential discussions with their clients if they are able to provide candid and effective legal advice," White House legal counsel Charles Ruff said in a statement.

The justices let stand a U.S. appeals court ruling that the attorney-client privilege does not apply to the notes, which had been subpoenaed by Whitewater independent counsel Kenneth Starr as part of his grand jury investigation.
"We regret that the court has decided not to resolve this important issue," Ruff said.
The Supreme Court's action, taken without any explanation or dissent, means the notes will have to be surrendered.

At issue are conversations Mrs. Clinton had on July 11, 1995, and on January 26, 1996, concerning her role in Whitewater. A White House lawyer took the notes while Mrs. Clinton talked with her private Whitewater attorney, David Kendall.
